{{Short description|Construction for simplicial sets}}
In [[higher category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''opposite simplicial set''' (or '''dual simplicial set''') is an operation extending the [[opposite category]] (or dual category). It generalizes the concept of inverting arrows from 1-categories to ∞-categories. Similar to the [[opposite category]] defining an [[Involution (mathematics)|involution]] on the [[category of small categories]], the opposite simplicial sets defines an involution on the [[category of simplicial sets]]. Both correspond to each other under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]] construction.

== Definition ==
On the simplex category <math>\Delta</math>, there is an automorphism <math>\rho\colon
\Delta\rightarrow\Delta</math>, which for a map <math>f\colon
[m]\rightarrow[n]</math> is given by <math>\rho(f)(i):=n-f(m-i)</math>. It fulfills <math>\rho^2=\operatorname{Id}</math> and is the only automorphism on the simplex category <math>\Delta</math>. By precomposition, it defines a functor <math>\rho^*\colon
\mathbf{sSet}\rightarrow\mathbf{sSet}</math> on the category of simplicial sets <math>\mathbf{sSet}
=\mathbf{Fun}(\Delta,\mathbf{sSet})</math>. For a simplicial set <math>X</math>, the simplicial set <math>X^\mathrm{op}
=\rho^*(X)</math>is its ''opposite simplicial set''.<ref name=":10">Lurie 2009, 1.2.1 The Opposite of an ∞-Category</ref><ref>Cisinski 2019, 1.5.7.</ref>

== Properties ==

* For a simplicial set <math>X</math>, one has:
*: <math>(X^\mathrm{op})^\mathrm{op}
\cong X.</math>
* For a category <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, one has:<ref>Cisinski 2019, Proposition 1.5.8.</ref>
*: <math>N(\mathcal{C}^\mathrm{op})
=(N\mathcal{C})^\mathrm{op}.</math>

* A simplicial set <math>X</math> is an [[∞-category]] if and only if its opposite simplicial set <math>X^\mathrm{op}</math> is.<ref name=":10" />
* A simplicial set <math>X</math> is a [[Kan complex]] if and only if opposite simplicial set <math>X^\mathrm{op}</math> is.
